item.text: Write a fictional status report for Project Pebble 14, a pretend internal library-booking trial. Total length: 6500 to 8500 ASCII characters, never more than 9000. Use SIX dated entries, around 1100 characters each; do not add extra entries. Describe a pretend pilot scope, an earlier missing cancellation path, its repair and checks, a remaining fictional limitation, and a current Captain decision about starting the pretend trial. If postponed, the trial does not start. All facts and names must be fictional. Include concrete mundane test notes to reach at least 6500 characters, then stop after entry six. No tools, headings outside the entries or setup commentary.

2026-10-18 - Project Pebble 14 Pilot Scope Finalized

The Project Pebble 14 library-booking trial targets the Riverside branch lending operations over eight weeks. The pilot will cover reservation holds for circulating materials (books, audiobooks, media discs), staff fulfillment workflows, and patron pickup flows through a new booking interface integrated into the existing catalog search. We are explicitly excluding periodicals, academic journals, and reference-only materials from this phase. The trial cohort is 340 active patrons divided into control (managed under current reserve process) and treatment (using the booking system). Infrastructure will run on dedicated staging servers with production data snapshots refreshed weekly. Initial rollout covers Monday through Friday 9 AM to 5 PM only; evening and weekend support deferred to phase two if pilot metrics justify expansion. Database schema modifications approved for the holds table to track booking timestamps, fulfillment status codes, and staff notes. API rate limits set to 50 requests per minute per patron to prevent accidental queue flooding. Success criteria: 85% booking completion within 48 hours of patron placement, zero data corruption events, and staff processing time reduced by 20% relative to manual reservation entry. The team established a war room with twice-daily standups on October 17th. Deployment rehearsal scheduled for October 22nd.

2026-10-25 - Cancellation Path Gap Identified in Hold Release Workflow

During integration testing yesterday afternoon, tester Miriam Chen discovered that patrons can place bookings and staff can fulfill them, but the interface offers no documented cancellation flow for patrons to withdraw their own holds before pickup. The system stores cancellation requests in the audit log but does not execute the actual release: the hold remains locked in the fulfillment queue even after a cancellation submission, blocking staff from reassigning the material to waiting patrons. This surfaced during scenario testing where Chen placed five test holds and attempted to cancel three. Two cancellations triggered silent failures (no error shown to patron, but hold persisted). One hold was manually cleared by staff, but that required direct database intervention. The third and fourth holds showed inconsistent UI state: the patron app indicated "cancelled" while backend records marked them "hold_active_pending_fulfillment". This blocks the trial start because we cannot guarantee data integrity for a live cohort. Scope includes only self-service cancellation before physical handoff; staff-initiated cancellations via the admin panel were tested separately and function correctly. Root cause: the cancellation handler was stubbed during initial build but never wired to the database commit layer. Impact assessment complete: approximately 15% of feature code paths exercise cancellation; without this, we risk unreleasable materials and frustrated patrons.

2026-11-01 - Cancellation Flow Remediation Underway

Development team deployed a fix targeting the hold release chain. Changes include: (1) adding a cancel_requested_at timestamp to the holds table to track intent separately from status transitions, (2) implementing a transactional state machine that moves holds from active to cancelled and immediately unlocks them for reassignment, (3) adding a confirmation email to patrons after successful cancellation, and (4) logging all cancellation events to an audit trail for staff review. Code review completed Friday evening with two minor requested changes: adding idempotency checks so duplicate cancellation requests do not create orphaned records, and ensuring cancelled holds do not appear in patron recommendations for future searches. Both changes implemented by Saturday afternoon. The cancellation endpoint now validates that the requesting patron ID matches the hold owner before processing any state change. Concurrent hold operations are serialized through a row-level lock to prevent race conditions where a hold is being fulfilled while a cancellation is in flight. Database migration script tested on a copy of production data to confirm no data loss and backward compatibility with existing holds. Team performed schema verification Sunday morning; all indices created successfully and query plans optimized. Deployment to staging environment completed, and the system passed basic smoke tests. Integration test suite expanded from 47 to 62 test cases to cover cancellation workflows. Three edge cases requiring attention have been logged as known issues for future sprints but do not block the current trial.

2026-11-02 - Cancellation Repair Verification and Test Results

Comprehensive testing completed across all cancellation scenarios. Test suite results: 58 of 62 tests passed; 4 remain under investigation due to timeout delays in concurrent cancellation attempts under simulated load. Load testing with 200 concurrent users placing and cancelling holds simultaneously revealed latency spikes in the 2.5 to 3.2 second range when more than 80 patrons triggered cancellations within a 10-second window. Nominal single-user cancellation latency is 180 milliseconds, well within acceptable bounds. The timeout failures occur only when the database connection pool reaches 95% capacity; these are not data corruption events but rather throttling under extreme concurrent load unlikely in normal Riverside branch operations (maximum historical concurrent patrons: 34). Miriam Chen re-ran all five of her original discovery scenarios: all cancellations now execute correctly, hold status updates propagate to the patron interface within 500 milliseconds, and staff see the released materials immediately in the reassignment queue. Two staff members (Gary Voss and Pam Ng) conducted end-to-end workflow testing in the staging environment Friday, completing 30 practice cycles of placement, fulfillment, and cancellation across different material types. Both reported the interface was intuitive and the workflow faster than the legacy manual process. Database audit trail was verified: all 92 test cancellations appear with correct timestamps and patron identifiers. Backup and restore procedures tested successfully Saturday evening; a full holds table snapshot and recovery completed in 4 minutes 15 seconds, within our 5-minute acceptable window. No data loss observed in any scenario.

2026-11-03 - Known Limitation: Concurrent Booking on Single Material

During load testing Friday, a fictional limitation emerged in the system behavior when multiple patrons attempt to book the same item simultaneously. The booking engine currently supports only sequential holds on individual copies; when a material has three physical copies and four patrons submit booking requests within the same second, the fourth patron receives a "no availability" response even though one copy technically remains unclaimed. The system lacks a dynamic re-queuing algorithm to assign the fourth patron to the next available copy or place them in a hold queue that auto-assigns when another copy arrives back in the system. This is a known design limitation accepted in the original requirements but not prioritized for the pilot phase. Impact: patrons may experience a perceived unavailability that contradicts the catalog display, requiring them to retry their booking within a few seconds for the system to recognize updated inventory. Staff have been trained to explain this behavior and assist patrons with manual rebooking if needed. The engineering team flagged this as a future optimization candidate (estimated effort: 8 to 12 engineering hours for a full queue-aware assignment algorithm). For the trial scope, we accept this limitation because Riverside branch average daily patron traffic is lower than the peak concurrent scenario that triggers the issue, and the workaround is simple. Monitoring will track how often patrons encounter this state and whether user satisfaction metrics are affected. If more than 3% of booking attempts result in spurious unavailability, the limitation will be reassessed before the phase-two expansion to other branches.

2026-11-04 - Captain Decision: Trial Start Approved with Monitoring Conditions

Captain Mitchell reviewed all test reports and repair verification findings yesterday morning and approved moving forward with the trial start. Trial launch date set for Monday, November 7, 2026, 9:00 AM at Riverside branch, targeting the full 340-patron cohort. Approval hinges on three monitoring conditions: (1) a dedicated on-call engineer assigned to the war room every day the trial is active to respond to data anomalies within 15 minutes, (2) an automated alert system configured to page the duty engineer if more than 10 consecutive cancellation operations fail or if the database connection pool exceeds 90% utilization, and (3) a twice-daily data integrity report comparing hold counts, fulfillment rates, and cancellation volumes against historical baseline to catch silent failures early. All conditions are now in place. The pilot will run for eight weeks, ending December 30, 2026, with interim review gates at weeks two and four. If at any point the integrity monitoring detects corruption, the trial will pause until root cause is understood and remediation verified. The control group (170 patrons) will continue using the existing manual reservation process managed entirely by staff through the legacy system. The treatment group (170 patrons) will use the new booking interface. Staff at Riverside have completed training and signed off on operational readiness. Staging infrastructure will remain live as a warm backup environment, refreshed daily from production data snapshots. The decision reflects confidence in the repair work verified through testing while acknowledging the concurrent booking limitation as an acceptable known risk for the eight-week window. Deployment to production is scheduled for Sunday evening after final pre-flight checks and staff briefing at 6 PM.
